articles.headline: Investor Interest Reignited in Electric Two-Wheeler Startups
articles.summary: Record adoption and sharp oil price increases have sparked a funding frenzy for electric two-wheeler startups. Zeno is in talks for $35-40 million, while others like River Mobility and Ultraviolette have recently secured large rounds. Investors view the sector as having crossed the adoption threshold, making fundraising easier than in previous years.

articles.headline: India Joins EAS Nations to Tackle Transnational Cybercrime
articles.summary: India has partnered with East Asia Summit members, including the US, China, and Russia, to combat online scams, money laundering, and human trafficking. The joint statement calls for intelligence-sharing and faster recovery of criminal proceeds. PM Modi proposed hosting an EAS Cyber Crime Conference at India's National Forensic Sciences University.

articles.headline: Xi Jinping Meets Trump in Rare Shenzhen Airport Arrival Greeting
articles.summary: In a rare diplomatic gesture, Chinese President Xi Jinping personally greeted US President Donald Trump at Shenzhen Airport. This is the first time in nearly 50 years a Chinese leader has met a visiting dignitary at the airport. The meeting occurs amid rising tensions over US curbs on China's access to high-end artificial intelligence technology.

articles.headline: Old Monk Maker’s Revenue Halves Following Sales Restrictions
articles.summary: Mohan Meakin, the maker of Old Monk, reported a 64% revenue decline in H1 after food safety authorities halted sales of three variants in Maharashtra. Regulators questioned the classification of the products as standard rum. The company withdrew a court challenge and plans to submit revised labels to FSSAI to resume operations at its Khopoli plant.

articles.headline: SpiceJet Cancels Over 50% of Flights Daily Amid Cash Crunch
articles.summary: SpiceJet is operating only about 15 of its 66 scheduled daily flights as a severe cash crunch forces the grounding of many aircraft. Despite the disruptions, the DGCA has not restricted the airline from taking forward bookings. The airline's board has approved raising up to Rs 5,500 crore, but executives warn that sustained operations require immediate funds.

articles.headline: Tata Sons Board to Discuss Mandatory Listing and RBI Compliance
articles.summary: Tata Sons will hold a board meeting on November 26 to address the RBI's mandate for the core investment company to list by 2026. Tensions remain between the holding company and Tata Trusts over staying private. The board will also review a presentation by Air India CEO Tewolde Gebremariam regarding the airline’s ongoing transformation and losses.

articles.headline: Niche Consumer Companies Plan Rs 10,000-12,000 Crore December IPOs
articles.summary: A diverse group of niche consumer firms, including Foodlink, Jerai Fitness, and Nobel Hygiene, are set to launch IPOs next month. Collectively seeking up to Rs 12,000 crore, these companies represent a record year for primary markets. Investors are showing increased interest in specialized segments like luxury catering, commercial gym equipment, and wellness.

articles.headline: Ind AS Amendments to Ease Hyperinflationary Currency Conversions
articles.summary: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs is likely to amend Indian Accounting Standard 21 to simplify how companies convert financial statements from hyperinflationary economies. Effective April 2027, the rules will require using the exchange rate at the reporting date for all items. The move aims to align Indian rules with international standards and ensure consistency.

articles.headline: ONGC to Ramp Up Deepwater Exploration as Mature Output Falls
articles.summary: ONGC plans to drill 13 exploratory wells in FY28, up from four this year, to counter a 6-8% natural production decline in mature fields. The focus is on deep and ultra-deepwater blocks under the Samudra Manthan initiative. High drilling costs and rig shortages remain challenges, with the company recently awarding contracts for specialized drillships.

articles.headline: Centre to Frame Selection Criteria for Sovereign Cloud Hosting
articles.summary: The government is developing tighter guidelines for hosting un-anonymized citizen data on cloud platforms to prevent cyber threats. Ministry of Electronics and IT officials are holding industry dialogues to establish selection criteria for sovereign cloud providers. The rules aim to ensure secure hosting for government systems containing personal citizen data.

articles.headline: US Billionaire’s Ivanhoe Atlantic Signs Mining Deal with Pakistan
articles.summary: Robert Friedland’s Ivanhoe Atlantic has signed a MoU with Pakistan’s Mari Minerals for greenfield exploration in Balochistan. The deal has raised red flags due to Friedland’s ties with Chinese state-owned entities CITIC and Zijin Mining. Mari Minerals is linked to the Pakistan military-run Fauji Foundation, which maintains deep commercial ties with Chinese firms.

articles.headline: NIA Arrests KZF Supporter Thikriwal After US Deportation
articles.summary: The National Investigation Agency arrested Surinder Singh, alias Thikriwal, at IGI Airport following his deportation from the US. Thikriwal is a supporter of the Khalistan Zindabad Force and is accused of involvement in a 2026 blast on a railway line in Punjab. He allegedly posted social media content glorifying the terror incident to disrupt communal harmony.

articles.headline: SC Issues Notice on Plea Against Political Protests in Delhi
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has issued notices to the Cockroach Janta Party, Congress, AAP, and AISA following a petition by Delhi traders. The traders allege that political demonstrations in the capital last month disrupted commercial activities and caused significant financial losses. The plea seeks court intervention to protect the right to carry on trade and business.

articles.headline: Court Seeks Report on Sonia Gandhi Voter List Complaint
articles.summary: A Delhi court has directed the police to submit an action-taken report regarding a complaint against Sonia Gandhi. The complaint alleges her name appeared on the New Delhi electoral rolls in 1980, three years before she acquired Indian citizenship in 1983. The court has requested original attested copies of the electoral records for further consideration.

articles.headline: Bengaluru Leads India in AI Startup Funding and Unicorns
articles.summary: A report by the Karnataka government reveals Bengaluru accounts for 36.3% of India's AI startup funding and 71% of AI unicorns created since 2023. The city has produced 57 unicorns valued at $211 billion. Bengaluru startups reach 'soonicorn' status in about five years, the fastest in the country, with significant growth in deep-tech and women-led ventures.

articles.headline: Karnataka Plans 1,000-Acre Startup Park Near Bengaluru
articles.summary: The Karnataka government will develop a 1,000-acre model startup park near Bengaluru and a 100-200-acre park in Hubballi-Dharwad. Industries minister MB Patil said the move aims to counter rising land costs and encourage manufacturing. The state is also considering an additional 5% subsidy for startups setting up operations outside the capital city.

articles.headline: Karnataka Flags Excess Ethanol in Petrol, Urges Policy Review
articles.summary: Karnataka has urged the Centre to review the E20 ethanol-blending program after state inspections found ethanol levels up to 31%, exceeding the 20% limit. The state government claims these variations indicate non-compliance by retailers and harm consumer interests. The letter also highlighted concerns regarding the quality and composition of premium petrol.

articles.headline: BJP Slams Rahul Gandhi for Defaming India Abroad
articles.summary: The BJP labeled Rahul Gandhi 'immature' and 'anti-India' following his remarks on the economy at Columbia University. Spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia accused Gandhi of a 'sinister design' to destabilize Indian democracy through baseless remarks on foreign soil. Union Minister Prahlad Joshi added that Gandhi's foreign trips are often used for anti-India propaganda.

articles.headline: Putin Pushes for Russia-India EAEU Trade Agreement
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin is advocating to fast-track a free trade agreement between India and the Eurasian Economic Union. Speaking at the APEC Summit, Putin highlighted Asia-Pacific as the global economic driver. Bilateral trade between India and Russia reached $55 billion in the first eight months of 2026, on track to hit a $100 billion target by 2030.

articles.headline: Darjeeling Tea Industry Struggles as Production and Exports Fall
articles.summary: Darjeeling tea production has plummeted from 14.49 million kg in 1990 to 5.6 million kg in 2025. The industry is struggling with aging bushes, climate change, and competition from cheaper Nepalese tea, which now sees 11.7 million kg imported into India. Experts warn the 'Champagne of teas' faces a survival crisis unless Nepalese imports are restricted.

articles.headline: Disney’s Share of JioStar Loss Narrows to $158 Million
articles.summary: The Walt Disney Company reported its equity loss from JioStar India narrowed by 22% to $158 million in fiscal 2026. The reduction is attributed to improved performance in the fourth quarter. JioStar, a joint venture between Disney and Reliance Industries, was formed following the merger of Viacom18 into Star India. Reliance continues to hold a controlling stake.

articles.headline: Companies Fear Escalating AI-Led Cyberattacks and Website Breaches
articles.summary: Businesses are increasingly concerned about AI-driven cyberattacks after incidents exposed vulnerabilities in digital infrastructure. Google flagged that AI can autonomously find and exploit software flaws. Experts warned that Indian websites loading third-party code for chat bots or analytics are at risk, with one breach potentially exposing credentials across 170 organizations.

articles.headline: Maharashtra FDA Suspends Licenses of Nine South Mumbai Eateries
articles.summary: The Maharashtra FDA has suspended the licenses of nine restaurants in South Mumbai, including Cafe Ideal and Bayroute, for hygiene and safety violations. Inspections revealed unhygienic preparation areas, pest infestations, and improper food storage. Additionally, food items worth Rs 1.27 crore were seized across the state for various regulatory violations.

articles.headline: Finance Ministry Maps Research and Development Spend Across Schemes
articles.summary: Ahead of the budget, the finance ministry is assessing R&D expenditures across all government programs to strengthen domestic capabilities. India's current R&D spending stands at 0.83% of GDP, significantly lower than the US and China. The exercise aims to provide a predictable funding framework for long-term technology projects in sectors like semiconductors and AI.

articles.headline: Market Stakeholders Seek LTCG and STT Relief in Pre-Budget Meet
articles.summary: Capital market representatives urged Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman to lower long-term capital gains tax and securities transaction tax. The mutual fund industry lobbied for tax parity between debt funds and equity funds. Other demands included enhancing liquidity for small NBFCs and reducing the threshold for enforcing security under the SARFAESI Act.

articles.headline: HDFC Capital Partners with Pecan Realty for Rs 1,000 Crore Project
articles.summary: HDFC Capital Advisors has joined forces with Pecan Realty to develop commercial and mixed-use properties in Mumbai. Their first project in Andheri East, valued at Rs 1,000 crore, will feature 400,000 sq ft of office and retail space. The partnership is structured as a long-term platform to create institutional-quality assets in established business districts.

articles.headline: Mahindra Last Mile Eyes Exports to Africa and Southeast Asia
articles.summary: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility plans to expand its electric three-wheeler exports to Africa and Southeast Asia over the next three years. The company targets one million EV sales by FY31 and is considering an IPO in about 18 months. Currently commanding a 36.2% domestic market share, the firm aims for exports to contribute 5% of its total sales volume.

articles.headline: Royal Enfield to Launch 250cc Bikes to Target Young Buyers
articles.summary: Royal Enfield is developing a new 250cc motorcycle platform to attract younger riders moving up from entry-level commuter models. The company aims to capture a larger share of the growing mid-weight motorcycle segment, which has doubled in volume over five years. The new models are expected to launch next fiscal as part of a premiumization strategy.

articles.headline: Cognizant Bags $175 Million IT Deal from UK Network Rail
articles.summary: Cognizant has secured a seven-year, $175 million contract from UK Network Rail Infrastructure for data centre and cloud platform services. Beating competitors like HCLTech and TCS, the firm will support government-owned railway networks and mainframe applications. The deal is part of a broader trend of vendor consolidation in the IT services industry.

articles.headline: InsuranceDekho Cuts 500 Jobs and Delays IPO After Merger
articles.summary: InsuranceDekho has seen 400-500 employees leave following its merger with RenewBuy as it looks to improve efficiency. The company has also postponed its planned Rs 3,000 crore IPO to rethink its business model amid proposed regulatory caps on distribution commissions. The firm continues to evaluate performance and align with changing Irdai guidelines.

articles.headline: Satya Nadella Vows to Improve Microsoft Security and AI Reliability
articles.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella stated the company is committed to continuous improvement following recent global outages. Speaking at the Ignite conference, he addressed the challenge of AI alignment, noting that the internal workings of scaling models remain elusive. Nadella emphasized that the company takes its global responsibility for secure infrastructure extremely seriously.

articles.headline: Sebi Chairman Rules Out Extending Market Trading Hours
articles.summary: Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey announced that the regulator has no plans to extend market trading hours, citing potential cybersecurity risks and costs. He also clarified that no decision has been taken to link Margin Trading Facility (MTF) limits to a stock's free float. The comments address recent debates triggered by US markets expanding their trading windows.

articles.headline: Small Loan Defaults Rise, Prompting Lenders to Tighten Norms
articles.summary: Housing finance and NBFC firms are tightening underwriting standards after rising repayment stress in loans below Rs 10 lakh. India Shelter Finance and Aptus Value Housing have flagged higher delinquencies among lower-income borrowers. Some lenders have stopped originating small-ticket loans against property to manage rising credit risks and borrower leverage.

articles.headline: India Champions Climate Finance Justice at COP31 Talks
articles.summary: At COP31, Union Minister Bhupender Yadav argued that developing nations should not choose between climate action and poverty reduction. He called on developed countries to discharge climate finance obligations and criticized unilateral trade measures. India insisted that the global south should not bear the burden of historical emissions from industrialized nations.

articles.headline: Air India Express Appoints Deepak Rajawat as New CEO
articles.summary: Deepak Rajawat, formerly the CFO of Air India Express, will take over as CEO on December 1. He succeeds Aloke Singh, who exited earlier this year. Rajawat, with two decades of aviation experience including roles at Vistara, will lead the budget carrier's expansion and fleet integration efforts as the Tata Group consolidates its low-cost operations.

articles.headline: Nvidia Q3 Revenue Doubles to $115 Billion Amid Investigation
articles.summary: American chipmaker Nvidia reported doubling its Q3 revenue to over $115 billion, driven by surging AI demand. Despite strong earnings, the company faces an SEC investigation into its financial disclosures. Leadership confirmed that former CEO Jensen Huang will not return, ending internal campaigns for his reinstatement. Shares remained under pressure due to long-term debt concerns.

articles.headline: No trade deal till US puts in place new tariff plan
articles.summary: India-US trade deal negotiations are stalled until the US establishes a new tariff architecture. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal stated that a deal cannot be signed without clarity on levy structures following US Supreme Court rulings and Section 301 probes. India aims to preserve comparative advantages while seeking a reciprocal tariff framework to resolve ongoing investigations.

articles.headline: Gold and silver crash to year's low on dollar strength
articles.summary: Gold and silver prices hit 14-month lows on Wednesday due to a strengthening US dollar and expectations of US Federal Reserve policy tightening. Pure gold closed at ₹1,31,164 per 10g, while silver plummeted to ₹1,63,733 per kg. Analysts suggest the correction may continue amidst global economic uncertainty and a stronger greenback affecting bullion demand.

articles.headline: Consumers remain value-conscious but willing to spend on quality
articles.summary: Westlife Foodworld, the operator of McDonald’s in West and South India, reported its strongest Q2 ever in FY27, driven by same-store sales growth. CEO Akshay Jatia noted that while consumers are value-conscious, they are willing to pay for premium quality and service. The company plans to add over 60 restaurants annually to reach 1,000 outlets by 2031.

articles.headline: UP tops two-wheeler sales while Maharashtra leads in PVs
articles.summary: Data from SIAM for Q2 2026-27 shows Uttar Pradesh leading in two and three-wheeler sales, with 7.89 lakh and 34,000 units respectively. Maharashtra led the passenger and commercial vehicle segments. Overall, the western zone had the highest market share in passenger vehicles (35.7%), while the northern zone led in two-wheeler sales with 12.1% market share.

articles.headline: SML Mahindra offers shares at 37% discount for rights issue
articles.summary: SML Mahindra is offering shares at a 37% discount for its ₹1,449.6 crore rights issue, priced at ₹3,506 per share. This move comes as majority shareholder Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) seeks to increase its stake in the commercial vehicle maker. M&M intends to invest approximately ₹855 crore in the issue, potentially raising its stake beyond its current 58.97%.

articles.headline: India’s CNG infrastructure could be its biggest net-zero advantage
articles.summary: A report by EY-CII suggests India’s CNG infrastructure, with 30,000 km of pipelines and 14,000 stations, provides a unique path to net-zero through Compressed Biogas (CBG). CBG can be used in existing CNG vehicles, potentially making India’s fleet carbon-negative. The report highlights that CBG offers significant life-cycle emission reductions compared to diesel fuel.

articles.headline: Dassault Systemes aims to scale India business to $1 billion
articles.summary: French software giant Dassault Systemes plans to grow its India business to $1 billion by focusing on startups and its 3DEXPERIENCE platform. The company is seeing 25% of its new commercial logos coming from India through startup programs. It currently serves 18,000-20,000 customers in India across automotive, aerospace, and industrial sectors.

articles.headline: SEBI mulls more safeguards for margin trading with no decision
articles.summary: SEBI Chairman Madhabi Puri Buch stated the regulator is considering additional safeguards for the margin trading facility (MTF) to manage risks from leveraged positions. Potential measures include restricting positions in stocks with low free float. The MTF book stood at ₹1.53 lakh crore in November, up 29% from last year, with high exposure in small and mid-cap stocks.

articles.headline: Softer oil and AI reset to boost India's growth: CEA
articles.summary: Chief Economic Advisor V. Anantha Nageswaran stated that lower oil prices and the global reset in AI valuations will support India's growth and FDI in FY28. He highlighted that despite a recent slowdown in foreign investment, India remains a preferred destination due to macroeconomic stability. He also noted that manufacturing grew by 9.2% in the first quarter of the year.

articles.headline: Firms turn to bond market as lenders raise interest rates
articles.summary: Indian companies are increasingly turning to the corporate bond market as banks raise their lending rates. Benchmark rates for 5-year bonds from entities like SIDBI, REC, and Tata Capital range from 7.9% to 8.5%. Analysts suggest that high borrowing costs and the transition to external benchmark linked rates are driving firms to seek cheaper financing through bonds.

articles.headline: Telangana seeks Centre's support for maize-based edible oil project
articles.summary: The Telangana government has proposed a ₹100-150 crore project to produce edible oil from maize. The state has sought the Union Agriculture Ministry’s help to set up an expert committee and conduct a feasibility study. The project aims to reduce India's 55% dependency on edible oil imports by utilizing Telangana's 305.09 lakh tonnes of annual maize production.

articles.headline: Petrol dealers to meet Minister today for margin hike demand
articles.summary: Petrol pump operators are scheduled to meet Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri to demand a revision of dealer commissions, which have been stagnant since 2017. Dealers argue that current margins are inadequate for single-shift operations and do not account for rising financial costs. Most retail outlets are reportedly operating at sales of less than 100 kilolitres per month.

articles.headline: Rupee pares early gains on RBI dollar supplies to OMCs
articles.summary: The Indian rupee ended slightly lower at 93.44 against the US dollar after early gains were offset by RBI's dollar sales to oil marketing companies. The local currency had initially strengthened due to inflows of ₹2,250 crore from institutional investors. Traders expect the rupee to remain in a range of 91.5-92.5 per dollar through December 2026 due to soft commodity prices.

articles.headline: Public sector banks record ₹1.1 lakh crore profit in H1
articles.summary: India's 12 public sector banks reported a combined net profit of ₹1.1 lakh crore for the first half of FY27, a 17% increase over the previous year. The growth was driven by improved asset quality and stronger capital adequacy. Operating profits grew by 14% to ₹1.81 lakh crore. The Ministry of Finance noted that gross NPA ratios for PSBs fell to 1.69% as of September 30.

articles.headline: Gujarat and Maharashtra lead India’s solar rooftop surge
articles.summary: The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana has reached 57 lakh installations nationwide, with Gujarat (3,523.98 MW), Maharashtra (3,336.54 MW), and Uttar Pradesh (3,231.59 MW) leading in capacity. These three states account for over half of the national total. The government has disbursed ₹6,437.53 crore in subsidies to promote residential solar power and reduce reliance on traditional energy.

articles.headline: MoD inks ₹1,976 crore deal with IAI for missile upgrades
articles.summary: The Ministry of Defence signed a ₹1,976 crore contract with Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) to upgrade the Barak-1 missile systems on Indian Navy ships. The project involves upgrading fire-control radars and software to enhance point-defense capabilities against aerial threats. Public sector units BEL and BDL will act as primary industry partners for the upgrade project.

articles.headline: Resignation of Nvidia CEO raises corporate governance concerns
articles.summary: The resignation of Nvidia's co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of personal misconduct has raised significant corporate governance concerns. The editorial explores the impact of his departure on the company’s leadership stability and global AI market position. It notes that a powerful founder’s success can create risks when leadership is challenged or suddenly changed.

articles.headline: Railway Ministry explores export of Vande Bharat trains to neighbors
articles.summary: The Indian Railway Ministry is exploring the export of indigenously developed Vande Bharat train sets to neighboring countries like Sri Lanka and Myanmar. While previous attempts were limited by track gauge differences and lack of electrification, new standard-gauge models could offer opportunities in markets like Thailand and Vietnam, following successful DEMU exports to Sri Lanka.

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit faces hurdles over leader absence and financing
articles.summary: As negotiators gather for COP31 in Turkey, the effectiveness of the summit is questioned given the absence of leaders from major carbon-emitting nations like the US and China. While nearly 200 countries are participating, the lack of consensus on fossil fuel phase-outs and a target of $300 billion annually in climate financing remains a significant hurdle to achieving warming goals.

articles.headline: Pulses and oilseeds production remains a challenge for Indian agriculture
articles.summary: Despite the Green Revolution, India's production of pulses and oilseeds has lagged behind wheat and paddy due to a lack of irrigation and effective procurement. Pulses are primarily grown in rainfed areas, leading to stagnant yields. Achieving self-sufficiency requires a shift in focus toward high-yielding varieties and better price support and research for these essential crops.

articles.headline: GTA VI release set to grip Indian gaming market
articles.summary: Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI is set for release in late 2026, marking a major milestone for the $480 million-unit selling franchise. The game will feature a return to Vice City and introduce new gameplay mechanics. Pre-orders in India have already surged, with gaming cafes reporting high demand for console bookings and accessories ahead of the highly anticipated launch.

articles.headline: FinMin directs ministries to identify unauthorized bank accounts
articles.summary: The Finance Ministry has directed all ministries and departments to identify bank accounts opened without proper authorization. This move aims to enhance the security of government banking operations and ensure funds are managed through prescribed channels. Departments must report any suspicious accounts and detail the actions taken to close or regularize them by January 2027.

articles.headline: Contract staffing in India outpaces permanent hiring in tech sector
articles.summary: A report by CIEL HR Services shows that contract staffing in India's technology sector grew by 10.1% in FY26, significantly outpacing permanent hiring. Companies are increasingly seeking project-based talent to manage fluctuating demands and specialized skills like AI and cybersecurity. The shift is driven by the need for flexibility and the rapid evolution of technology requirements.

articles.headline: ₹6,700 crore worth gold and silver held up at Customs
articles.summary: Over 5 tonnes of gold and silver, valued at approximately ₹6,700 crore, are currently stuck at Indian ports due to a delay in the update of tariff rates by the DGFT and CBIC. The delay has led to non-payment of duty, with customs levying interest on the unpaid amounts. Industry bodies are urging the Finance Ministry to rectify the Icegate system to allow for the clearance of goods.

articles.headline: CCI begins 2026-27 MSP purchase of cotton from Telangana
articles.summary: The Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) has started purchasing cotton under the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for the 2026-27 season in Telangana. The CCI has set up 600 centers to procure cotton, with prices for medium-staple cotton set at ₹8,667 per quintal. Market arrivals are expected to pick up as farmers anticipate higher prices due to lower national crop production estimates.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh amends semicon policy for 80% capital support
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government has amended its Semiconductor & Display Fabrication Policy 4.0 to provide up to 80% capital support for semiconductor projects. This includes a 50% contribution from the Centre and 30% from the state. The move aims to attract investments in ATMP (Assembly, Testing, Marking, and Packaging) units and R&D centers within the state’s electronic hubs.

articles.headline: Centre seeks more time for AAIB report on AI crash
articles.summary: The Union government has requested an additional two to three weeks from the Supreme Court to file the final report on the Air India Flight 171 crash. The delay is attributed to the need for a thorough investigation and the involvement of international experts. The crash at Ahmedabad airport resulted in the loss of 12 crew members and 229 passengers in July 2026.

articles.headline: Male police officers can handle women protesters says Delhi Police
articles.summary: The Delhi Police informed the Supreme Court that there is no legal bar preventing male police officers from handling women protesters during crowd-control operations. The affidavit stated that the primary duty of the police is to maintain law and order, and female officers are deployed when available. This response follows petitions alleging manhandling of protesters by male officers.

articles.headline: Ambani plans 1,600-satellite constellation to challenge Starlink
articles.summary: Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani is seeking global partners to build and launch a 1,600-satellite constellation to challenge Elon Musk's Starlink in India. The project aims to provide low-latency satellite broadband services by 2035. Reliance is currently in talks with US and European firms for satellite manufacturing and ground station equipment to support the network.

articles.headline: Profit-booking trims market gains as SEBI margin rules rattle investors
articles.summary: Indian markets witnessed profit-booking on Wednesday, with the Nifty50 falling 0.63% to 25,227.95. The sell-off was triggered by SEBI's proposed changes to margin-trading rules, which could impact leveraged positions in small and mid-cap stocks. Retail investors also reacted to hawkish signals from the US Federal Reserve, leading to a decline in consumer durable and jewelry stocks.

articles.headline: Juan Mata announces retirement at 38
articles.summary: Former Manchester United and Chelsea playmaker Juan Mata has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 38 after a notable international and club career.

articles.headline: Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race, becomes first Alaska Native woman
articles.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in Alaska, becoming the first Alaska Native woman elected to the US Senate. This win gives Democrats a 56-44 majority in the Senate.

articles.headline: Retiring EPFO subscribers may get monthly payouts
articles.summary: EPFO plans a systematic withdrawal plan for subscribers, allowing voluntary contributions and monthly payouts for existing members over 55. This proposal will be discussed by the central board.

articles.headline: Govt health spend per person in 4 northern states less than northeast
articles.summary: Government health expenditure per person in Bihar, UP, MP, and Jharkhand averages Rs 1,651, less than half the Rs 3,501 in the Northeast and a fourth of the Rs 7,209 in UTs. Southern states average Rs 2,960.

articles.headline: Snake catcher dies after handling venomous krait
articles.summary: Rahul Dandapat, a snake catcher known as 'Sarpabandhu', died from a black krait bite during a ritual in West Bengal. He was often engaged by state officials and had a large social media following.

articles.headline: Can an Italian on visa raise slogans against govt? SC to hear PIL
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will hear a PIL asking if an Italian visiting India on a conference visa can legally raise political slogans against the Election Commission and the government at an event in Hyderabad.

articles.headline: K'taka govt will be 1st customer for startups
articles.summary: Karnataka's 'Govt First Policy' makes the state government the first customer for startups developing tech solutions for governance. Selected startups get grants up to Rs 25 lakh and access to anonymized data.

articles.headline: Can Rahul get EC to answer 48 questions on oath?
articles.summary: Opposition leaders want the Supreme Court to allow 48 interrogatories (written questions) to seek sworn answers from the Election Commission on electoral roll revision procedures, alleging irregularities.

articles.headline: Forces kill Kashmir's last active local terrorist
articles.summary: Security forces killed 22-year-old Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Mohammad Lateef Bhat in Kulgam, ending the hunt for Kashmir's last known active local terrorist. Local recruitment into militant ranks has fallen significantly.

articles.headline: AI should help visually challenged learn science: Experts
articles.summary: Experts warn that AI absorbing entry-level tech jobs could threaten visually impaired students. They urge AI to be made accessible for higher-tier skills like science and math.

articles.headline: Drone racer wants to make flying 5-sec job
articles.summary: Devesh K Hedge is developing a business to make drone flying accessible, inspired by Elon Musk. His company Flycamp aims to simplify drone operation, making it a five-second job.

articles.headline: Switchgear factory to turn museum of innovation & tech
articles.summary: Bengaluru's disused NGEF switchgear factory will be transformed into India's first Museum of Innovation and Technology. The project aims to showcase India's innovation story from 1947.

articles.headline: GIS mapping to align property valuations with market rates
articles.summary: Karnataka plans to use GIS tech to align property guidance values with market rates, addressing disparities and boosting revenue. Property purchases may become costlier due to revised valuations.

articles.headline: MP to junk 2-child policy for its staff
articles.summary: Madhya Pradesh scrapped a 25-year-old rule barring state employees from having more than two children, citing falling fertility rates. The policy was introduced in 2001.

articles.headline: PM: Encourage savings, India doesn’t have ‘khao, piyo, mauj karo’ culture
articles.summary: PM Modi urged ministers to promote savings, stating India's culture isn't 'eat, drink, and have fun'. He also highlighted success in poverty reduction and combating Maoist threat.

articles.headline: PM Modi invokes Ramayana & Mahabharata, flags attacks on Hindu temples
articles.summary: PM Modi invoked Ramayana and Mahabharata, criticizing attacks on Hindu temples and alleged targeting of Sikhs. He urged communities to reject hate and uphold shared values.

articles.headline: Nvidia sets record with $65bn Q3 profit
articles.summary: Nvidia reported a record $65.3 billion profit in Q3, more than double its revenue of $115.8 billion. The company projects even higher revenue for the current quarter.

articles.headline: Govt teachers protest in UP, warn schools may shut
articles.summary: UP govt teachers protested, warning that large-scale deployment as BLOs and for Census duties could disrupt schools. They demand exemption from non-academic duties to ensure schools remain functional.

articles.headline: Keralam CM faces quizzing by ministers at cabinet meet
articles.summary: Keralam CM VD Satheesan faced questioning from ministers over PSC appointments and board positions. Differences were resolved through discussions, with ministers asserting their freedom to disagree.

articles.headline: Fighting alone, prof wins 26-yr court battle for teacher’s job
articles.summary: A 47-year-old Chandigarh professor won a 26-year legal battle for his medical reimbursement after a heart transplant. He will now be appointed as a Sanskrit teacher with backdated benefits.

articles.headline: Foreign money making healthcare costlier: Min
articles.summary: Health minister U T Khader expressed concern over corporate and foreign investment in healthcare potentially increasing treatment costs. He plans to write to the Centre on the issue.

articles.headline: 4 die as car crashes into goods vehicle
articles.summary: Four people died and two were injured when a speeding car collided with a Bolero goods vehicle on the Bengaluru-Hyderabad National Highway near Chadalapura.

articles.headline: ASHA workers stage protest, urge govt to hear their plight
articles.summary: ASHA workers protested at Freedom Park, demanding better remuneration and working conditions. They highlight long hours, meagre pay, and difficult working environments, impacting family support.

articles.headline: No third CM, DKS doing a good job: Parameshwara
articles.summary: Deputy CM G Parameshwara dismissed speculation of a CM change, stating DK Shivakumar is leading effectively. He emphasized the Congress's focus on returning to power in 2028.

articles.headline: E-khatas for 88 lakh rural properties by Dec 2027
articles.summary: Karnataka aims to issue e-khatas to 8.8 lakh rural properties by Dec 2026 and 80 lakh by Dec 2027, digitizing property records. This will help families lacking property documents.

articles.headline: Delink quota from census or expedite delimitation: CWP
articles.summary: Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians urged consensus to fast-track 33% women's reservation by delinking it from the Census or expediting delimitation, citing implementation delays.

articles.headline: EPFO to allow micro-contributions like tips
articles.summary: EPFO plans to allow voluntary micro-contributions like tips and gifts through a digital mechanism. This aims to help gig and unorganised sector workers save for long-term retirement.

articles.headline: Contempt proceedings against lawyer over CJI remarks
articles.summary: Supreme Court initiated contempt proceedings against advocate Pravin Singhal for allegedly making derogatory remarks against CJI Surya Kant and questioning his integrity during open court proceedings.

articles.headline: Army restores Ayushman regimental packages for senior officers
articles.summary: Army restored traditional regimental insignia for senior officers (Brigadier and above), allowing them to wear specific headgear and badges. This reverses the 2023 standardization policy.

articles.headline: Kerala HC to govt: No need to identify adopted children in official docus
articles.summary: Kerala High Court ruled that government documents need not specify if an heir is adopted, stating society accepts adopted children as their parents'. This upholds the principle of equal status.

articles.headline: MP suspends 6 cops for ‘decriminalise’ threat
articles.summary: Madhya Pradesh CM suspended six police personnel after a hotel video showed them threatening to plant drugs to frame a man. This incident highlights alleged misconduct and abuse of power.

articles.headline: AI from the frontier: Anthropic’s filing details AI progress
articles.summary: Anthropic's IPO filing suggests AI research is rapidly accelerating, with AI potentially finishing coding tasks in half the time. The company is making significant strides in AI development.

articles.headline: Alcaraz inches closer to last four
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz defeated Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 to move closer to a semifinal spot at the ATP Finals. He aims for his maiden ATP Finals title, extending his winning run to 11 matches.

articles.headline: Why Sabalenka’s meltdowns can’t be ignored
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka's emotional outbursts on court have drawn scrutiny. Her apologies and explanations suggest a need for better emotional regulation and consideration of opponent's feelings.

articles.headline: Delhi beats Karnataka in final
articles.summary: Delhi defeated Karnataka in the BCCI Senior Women's T20 Trophy final in Ahmedabad. Karnataka posted 175/8, but Delhi chased it down with five wickets, with Tanisha Singh scoring 77 not out.

articles.headline: Loud looking: Dating gets its new rulebook
articles.summary: Singles are embracing 'loud looking' by openly expressing interest in long-term relationships, countering frustration with situationships. 72% of Indians aged 18-45 prefer dating someone with whom they see a future.

articles.headline: Anne Hathaway welcomes third baby with husband Adam Shulman
articles.summary: Anne Hathaway and Adam Shulman have welcomed their third child. The actress was seen carrying the newborn, joining their two older sons, Jonathan and Jack.

articles.headline: AI stars hold for Nvidia, tells Jensen Huang thanks, but no thanks
articles.summary: Nvidia's board confirmed they do not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, despite his willingness to return. The company's strong performance continues amid the leadership transition.

articles.headline: Ali Fazal to headline Richie Mehta’s next
articles.summary: Ali Fazal will star as Dr Aziz in Richie Mehta's five-part adaptation of E M Forster's A Passage to India, filming in India. The cast includes Naseeruddin Shah and Shahana Goswami.

articles.headline: Classified US National Security Network Hit by Major Tech Outage
articles.summary: An internal National Security Agency (NSA) network used for classified communications, NSANet, went offline on Tuesday. The agency described the disruption as a result of routine maintenance. President Donald Trump downplayed the incident, stating such problems are inevitable. While internal systems were affected, the NSA claimed mission-critical capabilities remained fully operational.

articles.headline: Bishnoi Gang Member Harichand Jat Arrested in California
articles.summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested Lawrence Bishnoi gang member Harichand Jat, alias Harry Boxer, in California on November 6. US authorities revealed Jat was previously arrested in October 2024 for illegal entry but released without vetting. Indian agencies allege Jat coordinated criminal activities, including extortion and threats against celebrities, from overseas.

articles.headline: SC to Hear Petition Against Italian Politician Over Political Slogan
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will hear a plea seeking action against Italian political official Giacomo Filibeck for raising the slogan 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod' at an event in Telangana. The petitioner alleges Filibeck interfered in India’s democratic system. The plea also demands an apology from the Telangana government for organizing the Bharat Summit where the remarks were made.

articles.headline: MCD Estimates 2,000 Years for Comprehensive Delhi Building Audit
articles.summary: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) informed the Centre that a structural and fire safety audit of 4 million buildings would require 4 million man-hours. With 500 personnel, the preliminary survey alone would take over four years. The report follows a Home Ministry directive seeking a safety roadmap after recent building collapses in the capital.

articles.headline: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat Begins Three-Day Visit to Manipur
articles.summary: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat arrived in Imphal for a three-day organizational visit. Bhagwat will review the Sangh's activities, centenary celebrations, and social initiatives. The visit also focuses on service efforts for communities affected by ongoing violence in the state. He last visited Manipur in November 2025.

articles.headline: Three Workers Killed in Conveyor Belt Collapse at NTPC Jharkhand
articles.summary: A collapse of an under-construction conveyor belt structure at NTPC’s North Karanpura project in Chatra district killed three workers and injured two others on Wednesday. The accident occurred when a counterweight broke during construction. Police suspect a design flaw and have initiated a probe. The deceased were identified as Raju Soni, Bablu Singh, and Baleshwar Paswan.

articles.headline: Voyager 1 Reaches Historic One Light-Day Milestone from Earth
articles.summary: Nasa’s Voyager 1 probe has reached a distance of one light-day from Earth, approximately 26 billion kilometres away. Launched in 1977, it is the most distant human-made object. Despite its age, recent power-saving measures may allow the spacecraft to continue communicating with Earth for another three to four years as it travels through interstellar space.

articles.headline: Delhi Police Seek Rerouting of Transit Traffic via Google Maps
articles.summary: Delhi Traffic Police plan to request Google Maps to stop showing the capital as a preferred route for vehicles not destined for the city. The move follows CAQM directives to reduce vehicular pollution and congestion. Authorities want transit traffic diverted to peripheral corridors. Meetings with traders are also underway to implement one-way traffic in major markets.

articles.headline: Delhi CM Warns Against Negligence as Air Quality Remains 'Poor'
articles.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta warned civic agencies against negligence as the city's AQI reached 232, remaining in the 'poor' category for the fourth day. Civic bodies were directed to intensify mechanized sweeping, road washing, and water sprinkling. The Air Quality Early Warning System has forecasted a deterioration to 'very poor' air quality by Friday.

articles.headline: Parallel Electricity Distribution Licence Put on Hold in Haryana
articles.summary: The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) refused immediate relief to Eleven Power Pvt Ltd regarding a stay on its parallel-distribution licence in Gurugram and Nuh. The Haryana government exercised special powers to halt the licence in public interest following worker strikes. APTEL has directed respondents to file replies within two weeks.

articles.headline: Allahabad HC Freezes New Construction at Jaypee Greens Golf Course
articles.summary: The Allahabad High Court ordered an immediate freeze on all new construction and third-party rights across 236.87 acres at Jaypee Greens Golf Course in Greater Noida. The order follows a petition by members alleging the land, meant for a golf course and clubhouse, was being misused for residential villas and condominiums. The court will hear the matter again on December 7.

articles.headline: Law Student Arrested for Stealing ₹30 Lakh from Grandfather
articles.summary: A 22-year-old law student, Abhishek Raghav, and his friend were arrested for siphoning nearly ₹30 lakh from his 87-year-old grandfather’s bank account. The accused allegedly used the funds for luxury trips to Manali and Nainital and to buy a car. The victim, a retired Navy official, discovered the fraud after noticing unauthorized transfers over a seven-month period.

articles.headline: Sarai Kale Khan Station Slated for Major Commercial Development
articles.summary: The NCRTC has invited bids to develop 21,063 square metres of buildable space above the Sarai Kale Khan Namo Bharat station. The project will utilize 'air-rights' to create hotels, offices, and retail outlets. The development aims to transform the transit hub, which records the highest footfall on the Delhi-Meerut RRTS corridor, into a mixed-use commercial destination.

articles.headline: Delhi Reconstitutes Councils for Five Language Academies
articles.summary: The Delhi government appointed 101 members to the governing councils of five language academies to promote the capital’s linguistic heritage. Academies for Hindi, Sanskrit, Punjabi, Maithili-Bhojpuri, and Garhwali-Kumaoni-Jaunsari were reconstituted. Art and Culture Minister Kapil Mishra will chair the councils, which include scholars and cultural figures serving two-year terms.

articles.headline: DDA and INTACH to Digitize Access to 1,500 Heritage Sites
articles.summary: The DDA and INTACH will document 1,500 heritage structures in Delhi to improve public accessibility. The initiative includes installing QR codes and information plaques at lesser-known monuments and historic bazaars. The project aims to create a comprehensive digital e-book and interactive maps to support conservation and cultural tourism under the Master Plan for Delhi 2047.

articles.headline: New Mental Health Policy for Delhi Schools to Address Crisis
articles.summary: The Delhi government will launch a mental health policy for schools and higher educational institutions on November 19. The policy mandates one counsellor for every 500 students and establishes a six-level crisis response mechanism. Schools must keep students at immediate risk of self-harm under adult supervision and are prohibited from promising secrecy regarding safety concerns.

articles.headline: Satish Gujral Murals to be Relocated to Jantar Mantar Area
articles.summary: Iconic ceramic-tile murals created by artist Satish Gujral in 1968 for Shastri Bhawan are set to be relocated to a site near Jantar Mantar. The NDMC and National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) are finalizing the installation near Palika Kendra. The 73-foot-tall murals, featuring abstract motifs and tribal art, were removed to ensure their preservation and public accessibility.

articles.headline: Yogi Adityanath Defends Slogan as Pitch for Social Caution
articles.summary: UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath defended his 'batoge toh katoge' (if divided, you will suffer) slogan, stating it is about remaining alert to lawlessness. Addressing an event in Lucknow, he urged Gen Z and Gen Alpha to learn about the state's past riots and insecurity. He claimed his 80:20 political formula represents those supporting development versus those supporting rioters.

articles.headline: UP Cabinet Approves Ordinance to Defer Panchayat Elections
articles.summary: The Uttar Pradesh cabinet promulgated an ordinance to extend the tenure of panchayat administrators by six months, effectively deferring elections. Finance Minister Suresh Khanna said the amendment to the UP Panchayat Raj Act allows more time for preparations. The move follows a previous High Court directive to hold local body elections within a three-month timeframe.

articles.headline: Centre Notifies New Prison Regulations for Andaman and Nicobar Islands
articles.summary: The Centre has notified the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Prisons and Correctional Services Regulation, 2026, replacing three colonial-era laws from 1894, 1900, and 1950. Based on a 2023 model act, the new law incorporates safeguards against discrimination and provides a three-year prison term for inmates caught using mobile phones or other prohibited communication devices.

articles.headline: ICMR Launches Syndromic Surveillance Grid to Track Outbreaks
articles.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has launched a syndromic surveillance initiative across 70 laboratories to provide early warnings for infectious disease outbreaks. The network will use real-time health data to detect pathogens causing fever, respiratory illness, and diarrhoeal disease. The system aims to determine the speed and size of potential outbreaks rapidly.

articles.headline: Madhya Pradesh Scraps Two-Child Norm for Government Jobs
articles.summary: The Madhya Pradesh cabinet, chaired by CM Mohan Yadav, approved the removal of the two-child rule for government employment. The decision ends a 25-year-old provision and withdraws pending disciplinary proceedings against employees for having more than two children. The cabinet also cleared investment proposals worth ₹70,650 crore across various sectors including pharma and solar energy.

articles.headline: Former TN Minister Named in ₹1,427-Crore Sand Mining Case
articles.summary: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption has named former Tamil Nadu minister Durai Murugan and several officials in an illegal sand mining case. The FIR alleges collusion resulted in a ₹1,427-crore loss to the exchequer between 2021 and 2024. The probe covers 28 quarry sites where mining was reportedly conducted at the instance of Murugan, a senior DMK leader.

articles.headline: Global South Rejects Burden of Historical Emissions at COP31
articles.summary: Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav, delivering India’s national statement at COP31 in Antalya, asserted that the Global South cannot bear the burden of addressing consequences of historical emissions. He called for climate action rooted in equity and the principle of 'Common But Differentiated Responsibilities'. Yadav also opposed unilateral trade measures penalized under climate guises.

articles.headline: Princess Catherine Wears Indian Designer at Earthshot Prize Awards
articles.summary: UK’s Princess Catherine (Kate Middleton) wore a vermilion-red Anarkali by Delhi-based designer Mahima Mahajan at the Earthshot Prize Awards in Mumbai. The outfit, modified with a trail and glass beads for sustainability, was paired with Queen Elizabeth II’s emerald jewels. Prince William accompanied her in a black velvet bandhgala designed by Manish Malhotra.

articles.headline: Electric trucks gain traction in India driven by corporate adoption
articles.summary: Electric trucks are seeing increased adoption in India, driven by large enterprises like Amazon and UltraTech Cement. Factors like range constraints, high costs, and infrastructure are being addressed. Corporate ESG goals and lower running costs offset upfront prices, making them viable for sectors like cement and ports. Challenges remain in scaling local manufacturing and expanding charging networks.

articles.headline: Indian economy shows warning signs in October; producer segment resilient
articles.summary: India's economic scorecard deteriorated in October, with 10 of 16 high-frequency indicators below their one-year averages. Pockets of resilience are in the producer economy, particularly credit growth. However, retail inflation breached the 6% tolerance limit. Challenges ahead include moderating GDP growth in H2 FY27 due to adverse rainfall and rising inflation.

articles.headline: Indian companies stage broad earnings recovery in Q2 FY27, strongest in three years
articles.summary: Indian companies saw a broad earnings recovery in Q2 FY27, with aggregate net profit up 30% year-on-year, the strongest in three years. This was driven by robust sales and a favourable statistical base. However, profit margins are retreating from last year's highs due to rising costs, raising concerns about sustained momentum.

articles.headline: Soya bean oil's share rises in India's edible oil import mix
articles.summary: India's soya bean oil imports are rising, increasing its share in the edible oil import mix. This shift is influenced by competitive pricing, disruptions in Black Sea supplies, and diversification efforts. Crude palm oil remains the largest import, but soya bean oil shows significant growth.

articles.headline: Govt better its rural worker grievance redressal framework
articles.summary: The government has launched a new grievance redressal framework under the Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025. This aims to ensure timely hearing and resolution of complaints from rural workers regarding job cards, wages, and other entitlements.

articles.headline: Centre eases export support rules, ups aid for small exporters
articles.summary: The commerce ministry has expanded eligibility for export support programs, allowing more small and medium exporters to claim reimbursements for trade promotion, quality certifications, and logistics costs. This aims to improve competitiveness and market access for Indian MSMEs.

articles.headline: India calls for equitable global climate action at COP31
articles.summary: India urged equitable global climate action at COP31, stating it's unjustified to expect developing nations to bear the burden of historical emissions. It stressed that climate cooperation must be based on equity, differentiated responsibilities, and respective capacities.

articles.headline: Bhim app focuses on repeat users over market share
articles.summary: Bhim app is prioritizing building a base of active, repeat users rather than chasing market share from rivals like PhonePe and Google Pay. It aims for gradual growth by focusing on products that encourage repeat use, including NPS investments and RuPay credit card payments.

articles.headline: NSE takes equity options playbook to commodity F&O
articles.summary: The National Stock Exchange is adopting a playbook similar to equity derivatives for commodity derivatives, specifically revising expiry dates for crude oil options. This move aims to attract more participants and increase turnover in the commodity derivatives market.

articles.headline: Cummins faces margin compression due to cost inflation and project execution
articles.summary: Cummins India is experiencing steep margin compression in Q2 FY27 due to severe cost inflation in raw materials and higher freight rates. Delayed pass-through of costs and execution of older projects at fixed prices have impacted gross and EBITDA margins. Price hikes are being implemented to mitigate the impact.

articles.headline: Ashok Leyland investors wary despite solid Q2 demand and revenue growth
articles.summary: Ashok Leyland's shares fell despite solid Q2 FY27 earnings and revenue growth. Investors are wary due to sustained cost pressures, including raw material costs, and potential profit-taking. The company maintained its mid-teen EBITDA margin guidance and plans for future growth, but market sentiment remains cautious.

articles.headline: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO: profits versus risks to be assessed
articles.summary: Mahanadi Coalfields is heading for an IPO worth ₹8,981 crore, consisting entirely of an offer for sale. While it's Coal India's most profitable subsidiary with substantial reserves, investors need to assess growth stagnation, reliance on FSAs, and potential regulatory dues despite strong financials.

articles.headline: Cognizant, Infosys eye GCC business with divergent AI strategies
articles.summary: Cognizant is focusing on workforce AI training for Global Capability Centers (GCCs), while Infosys is modernizing legacy technology and selling AI agents. Both are competing for GCC business, with Cognizant emphasizing talent transformation and Infosys on tech modernization and large deals. Their strategies differ significantly in approach to AI adoption.

articles.headline: WISE CEO flags ₹25 lakh RBI cap on cross-border payments
articles.summary: Kristo Käärmann, co-founder of WISE, questions RBI's ₹5 lakh cap on cross-border payments for exporters, arguing it hinders businesses. He suggests the government should help firms bring more money into India. The limit applies to PA-CB firms, impacting fintechs and cross-border startups.

articles.headline: SpiceJet plans ₹5,500 cr raise, more than its reported debt
articles.summary: Cash-strapped SpiceJet plans to raise ₹5,500 crore through share sales or loans, exceeding its total debt. The airline aims to rebuild operations and restore its brand. The fundraising is crucial amid a challenging aviation environment and low market share.

articles.headline: Nostalgia strikes a chord in the business of music
articles.summary: Old music catalogues from the 1980s-2000s are generating significant revenue for labels through sync licensing, films, and brand campaigns. Nostalgia appeals to consumers facing decision fatigue, making familiar songs valuable assets in a competitive music market.

articles.headline: Listed flex operators grow as firms seek office flexibility
articles.summary: Flexible and managed office operators are expanding across cities as enterprises and GCCs seek workspace flexibility. Companies like Smartworks, IndiQube, and Awfis reported revenue growth in H1 FY27, driven by higher leasing and rental escalations. Demand is expected to strengthen further.

articles.headline: Battery shift opens up new market for Bajaj, Mahindra
articles.summary: Stricter e-rickshaw regulations, including mandatory lithium-ion battery packs, are pushing drivers towards larger electric and CNG autos. Bajaj Auto and Mahindra & Mahindra are positioned to benefit from this shift as demand for formal three-wheelers rises.

articles.headline: Tata Steel's domestic capacity chase may be delayed by European transition
articles.summary: Tata Steel's plan to expand its Indian steelmaking capacity to 40 million tonnes by 2030 might slip due to the cost of transitioning its European operations to cleaner steelmaking. The company is balancing domestic growth ambitions with the financial sustainability of its European business.

articles.headline: New contract brings insurers, hospitals under single umbrella
articles.summary: India's insurance industry is simplifying hospital-insurer relations through a common empanelment system and a new dispute-resolution forum. This aims to streamline cashless treatment, reduce administrative burden, and resolve disputes more effectively.

articles.headline: Digital butlers at your fingertips: AI assistants manage Indian lives
articles.summary: Personal AI assistants like Ira and Littl are gaining traction in India, managing tasks from alarms to bookings. Indian startups are tailoring AI to local contexts like language and commerce. While offering convenience, concerns remain about privacy, security, and the potential for AI to become gatekeepers.

articles.headline: Anthropic approaches final IPO hurdle after tech stocks churn
articles.summary: AI model maker Anthropic is poised for potentially the biggest IPO of all time, aiming for a valuation of $1.4 trillion. Despite tech stock volatility, demand is strong, driven by the company's focus on healthcare and life sciences, and its strategic partnership with Nvidia.

articles.headline: Boutique consultancy firms challenge big ones at B-schools
articles.summary: Boutique consultancy firms are competing strongly with global strategy consultancies and Big Four firms for top talent at Indian business schools. They offer competitive compensation, brand value, and diverse work opportunities, attracting students seeking high-impact careers.

articles.headline: ACME clears $3.6 bn green fuel facility investment decision
articles.summary: ACME Group has finalized its $3.6 billion green ammonia project in Odisha, India. The facility, expected by 2029, will operate entirely on renewable energy, adhering to European standards for green fuel production.

articles.headline: Aragen to invest ₹1,500 cr in expansion over 3 years
articles.summary: Aragen Life Sciences plans to invest ₹1,500 crore over three years to expand its drug development and manufacturing business. This move aims to capitalize on growing global demand for outsourcing from pharmaceutical companies.

articles.headline: PW eyes ₹10,000 cr revenue by FY30 on strong digital learning demand
articles.summary: Physicswallah (PW) expects to achieve revenues of ₹9,000-10,000 crore by FY30, driven by demand for digital learning. The edtech platform aims for over 20% operating profit margin and sustained revenue growth, supported by a diversified course mix.

articles.headline: India, Italy should target €50 billion in trade: Goyal
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal proposed a €50 billion trade target for India and Italy, citing significant potential for economic ties. He emphasized leveraging the EU-India Free Trade Agreement to open new opportunities for businesses.

articles.headline: EQT weighs sale of IVF chain Indira
articles.summary: Private equity firm EQT AB is considering selling Indian fertility services provider Indira IVF Hospital Ltd, potentially valuing it at over $1.5 billion. The firm is exploring options and may decide on a sale after assessing market interest.

articles.headline: Cloudy view dulls Q2 earnings cheer; margins face pressure
articles.summary: Indian companies reported a strong Q2 FY27 earnings recovery, but rising costs are squeezing margins. While revenue grew robustly, profit margins declined year-on-year due to increased input costs, impacting profitability across sectors. Banks remain well-positioned to benefit from rising interest rates.

articles.headline: India's urban expansion a case of a glass half empty
articles.summary: Despite Bengaluru's metro expansion, Indian cities face challenges like poor waste management, air pollution, and traffic gridlock. Unlike China's managed urban development, Indian cities often suffer from a lack of effective leadership and administrative focus, highlighting systemic issues.

articles.headline: India's build-up for AI governance has progressed well
articles.summary: India has made progress in implementing AI governance guidelines since their release, focusing on infrastructure, capacity building, regulation, and accountability. Initiatives like AIKosh, DEPA, and sector-specific rules show a commitment to responsible AI adoption.

articles.headline: Caste, political pressure impact telecom reforms in India
articles.summary: J.S. Deepak's memoir 'I Dared to Dial Differently' details how caste, political pressure, and institutional shortcomings influenced telecom reforms, including the 2G scam. It highlights the challenges faced by civil servants in navigating power dynamics and upholding transparency.

articles.headline: Andrew Scott honors Ian Charleson in 'Elsinore'
articles.summary: Andrew Scott's performance in 'Elsinore' as Ian Charleson, battling AIDS while performing Hamlet, explores the intersection of art and mortality. The play honors Charleson's memory and Scott's powerful portrayal highlights vulnerability and resilience.

articles.headline: Sitar maestro Ravi Shankar's mind explored in 'Enchantment' play
articles.summary: Gowri Ramnarayan's play 'Enchantment' delves into the personal life and vulnerabilities of sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar, beyond his iconic status. It uses original recordings and dance to map his creative journey and internal struggles.

articles.headline: Front Page Lead: Economic Reforms Discussion
articles.summary: Lead story covers in-depth discussions on new economic reforms and policy changes. Analysts weigh in on potential impacts on various sectors and the national economy. Key stakeholders are reportedly involved in consultations, shaping the future financial landscape for sustained growth and development.

articles.headline: New Business Investment Initiatives
articles.summary: Article details initiatives to boost business investments, focusing on stimulating growth in key industries. Outlines government support measures and private sector participation targets for the coming fiscal year, projecting significant capital inflows to various sectors.

articles.headline: Infrastructure Project Updates Revealed
articles.summary: Updates on critical infrastructure projects across the nation. Discusses progress, funding, and anticipated completion dates. Emphasizes their role in regional development, enhancing connectivity, and boosting economic activity in diverse geographical areas.

articles.headline: Brief: Regulatory Changes Announced
articles.summary: Report on new regulatory changes affecting small and medium enterprises. Aims to streamline processes and reduce compliance burdens, fostering a more business-friendly environment for growth and expansion across various segments of the economy.

articles.headline: Local Business Growth Report
articles.summary: Report focuses on local business growth initiatives, highlighting successful case studies and community involvement. Details how local enterprises leverage opportunities and contribute to regional economic stability and employment generation at the grassroots level.

articles.headline: Global Trade Relations Impacting Local Markets
articles.summary: Article examines how evolving global trade relations are creating ripple effects in local markets. Discusses import-export dynamics, tariff adjustments, and international agreements influencing domestic prices and supply chains, affecting consumer goods and raw materials.

articles.headline: Technological Advancements in Banking
articles.summary: Recent technological advancements transform the banking sector, improving efficiency and customer experience. Explores adoption of AI, blockchain, and digital platforms in financial services, highlighting their transformative potential for secure and faster transactions.

articles.headline: Energy Sector Policy Revisions
articles.summary: Government announces new policy revisions for the energy sector, aiming for sustainable growth and increased domestic production. Details incentives for renewable energy and regulations for traditional sources, ensuring long-term energy security and environmental compliance.

articles.headline: Manufacturing Output Shows Robust Growth
articles.summary: Latest figures indicate robust growth in manufacturing output, exceeding projections. Sector's resilience attributed to increased consumer demand and strategic government support. Key sub-sectors are experiencing significant expansion and job creation.

articles.headline: Education Sector Reforms Underway
articles.summary: Major reforms implemented in the education sector to enhance quality and accessibility. Covers new curriculum developments, teacher training programs, and digital learning initiatives designed to modernize schooling across all levels and regions.

articles.headline: Digital Payments See Unprecedented Surge
articles.summary: Digital payments sector witnessed unprecedented surge, driven by increasing smartphone penetration and e-commerce adoption. Details growth metrics, consumer behavior shifts, and regulatory frameworks supporting the trend for secure and convenient transactions.

articles.headline: Corporate Governance Reforms Discussed
articles.summary: Discussions on corporate governance reforms highlight the need for greater transparency and accountability. Covers proposed changes to board structures, executive compensation, and shareholder rights, fostering investor confidence and ethical business practices.

articles.headline: Small Business Support Programs
articles.summary: Government launches new support programs for small businesses, including access to credit and mentorship. Aims to help startups and existing enterprises navigate economic challenges, expand operations, and foster job creation in local communities.

articles.headline: Export Growth Strategies Unveiled
articles.summary: New strategies to enhance export growth unveiled, targeting key international markets. Outlines government support for exporters, trade agreements, and diversification plans to boost national export volumes and strengthen trade balances.

articles.headline: Digital Transformation in Public Services
articles.summary: Public services undergo significant digital transformation for efficiency and accessibility. Details new e-governance initiatives, online portals for citizen services, and technology use to streamline administrative processes, improving public interaction.

articles.headline: Youth Employment Schemes Launched
articles.summary: Several new youth employment schemes launched, focusing on skill development and vocational training. Aims to equip young people with market-relevant skills, facilitating workforce entry and reducing unemployment rates across urban and rural areas.

articles.headline: Real Estate Market Outlook: Stable Growth
articles.summary: Real estate market shows stable growth, driven by sustained demand and favorable interest rates. Outlook predicts continued investment in residential and commercial properties, with developers adapting to evolving consumer preferences and market dynamics.

articles.headline: Healthcare Infrastructure Expansion
articles.summary: Plans for expanding healthcare infrastructure underway, with new hospitals and clinics planned for underserved regions. Aims to improve access to medical facilities and enhance the overall capacity of the healthcare system, especially in rural areas.

articles.headline: National Economic Outlook Positive
articles.summary: National economic outlook remains positive, with key indicators pointing to continued recovery and growth. Government policies credited with fostering a stable environment for businesses and investors, projecting a steady GDP increase and job creation.

articles.headline: Agricultural Subsidies Increased
articles.summary: Government announces increased subsidies for the agricultural sector to support farmers and boost productivity. Measures aim to reduce input costs, encourage modern technologies, and ensure fair prices for produce, strengthening the rural economy.

articles.headline: Public-Private Partnerships in Development
articles.summary: Role of public-private partnerships (PPPs) in accelerating national development projects highlighted. Discusses successful PPP models in infrastructure, technology, and social services, emphasizing their efficiency and innovation potential for sustainable growth.
